record.file_problem: README and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The repository uses directional ablation for targeted fact unlearning and cites the refusal-direction work, but it reports no refusal measurements.
record.gate_note: README results measure retained accuracy on target facts, not refusal of harmful requests or refusal of harmless requests. The listed result files were not read; no README-reported result tests a claim version.
record.test_reason: The repository borrows the difference-in-means ablation technique from the refusal-direction work and applies it to fact unlearning. It measures retained target-fact accuracy, never refusal of harmful or harmless prompts, so its results do not bear on any refusal-direction version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README says directional ablation strongly reduces target-fact accuracy on memorized knowledge, up to about 90%. It is weaker and setting-sensitive for broad entity-averaged forgetting. Collateral damage and comparisons against unlearning baselines are not yet measured.
record.recipe_differences: This is a fact-unlearning application, not a refusal-direction test. It forms a normalized mean difference between true-answer and perturbed-answer prompts, reads activations at a chosen layer and token position, and subtracts the direction during generation. The README describes the repository as built on directional-ablation/activation-steering work.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports that forgetting varies with intervention layer and strength (α), and says broad synthetic-wikidata results are setting-sensitive. It does not give values for the α sweep in the README.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating a normalized true-answer minus perturbed-answer mean-difference direction during generation lowers retained target-fact accuracy in Llama-3-8B settings. Retained accuracy falls 100%→9% on TOFU-tuned and 91%→65% on synthetic-wikidata. Collateral capability effects were not measured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Difference-in-means directional ablation, borrowed from refusal-direction work, can suppress specific factual recall in Llama-3-8B. Its strength depends on dataset, model stage and layer.

record.problems: The README says collateral damage to general capabilities has not been measured, there are no comparisons to standard unlearning baselines, the LLM judge is self-graded and unvalidated against human labels, and the older substring metric can disagree by up to ~10×. It also describes the project as a research prototype and flags cross-model transfer as open.
record.rows_left_out: Other result files and plots listed in the repository file list were not read, so their contents were not extracted. The README mentions α and perturbation sweeps but does not report their results as numbers in the text.

untested.parts: All parts: refusal ablation, refusal induction, capability retention.
All parts: no weight edit and no refusal measure.
All parts. Cross-model transfer is listed as open.

record.verdict_notes: This is a GitHub prototype with an unvalidated LLM judge. It cites Arditi et al. only as the source of the method. The repository name says 'abliteration', but it does not apply abliteration to refusal.
